cases.text: I think p.s. stands for postscript in formal writing.
cases.note: Inline 'p.s.' mid-sentence. No ^ anchor, so the shipped pattern finds it and passes a response that contains no actual postscript.

cases.text: PS I forgot to mention the meeting is at noon.
cases.note: 'PS' with no dots is a legitimate postscript spelling, but the shipped pattern hard-codes 'p.' and 's.' literal dots, so it fails.

cases.text: P.S I will call you tomorrow afternoon.
cases.note: 'P.S' (no trailing dot) is a legitimate spelling; the shipped pattern requires 's.' so it fails.

cases.text: P.S: remember to bring the signed documents.
cases.note: 'P.S:' with a colon is a legitimate spelling; the shipped pattern requires 's.' so it fails.

cases.text: P.S. Thanks again for all your help.
cases.note: Canonical 'P.S.' at line start. Both pass; control.

cases.text: Psychology is a fascinating field of study.
cases.note: 'Psychology' starts with 'ps'. Both fail; the intended guard (?![a-z]) keeps it from matching. Control.
